topic: How Bloom filters answer 'have I seen this before?' with very little memory

facts.fact: a bit array plus several hash functions
false positives possible, false negatives impossible
about 10 bits per item for a 1% false positive rate
standard filters cannot delete; counting Bloom filters can

search_results.title: Bloom filters in one page
search_results.snippet: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic set. It stores an array of m bits, all zero at first, and uses k independent hash functions. To add an item you hash it k times and set those k bits to 1.

search_results.title: Checking membership
search_results.snippet: To check an item, hash it the same k ways. If any of those bits is 0 the item was definitely never added, so there are no false negatives. If all are 1 it was probably added: other items may have set the same bits, which is a false positive.

search_results.title: How big should my Bloom filter be?
search_results.snippet: The false positive rate depends on bits per item and the number of hash functions. A useful rule of thumb: about 10 bits per item with 7 hash functions gives roughly a 1% false positive rate, no matter how large each item is.

search_results.title: Where Bloom filters are used
search_results.snippet: Databases built on LSM trees keep a Bloom filter per data file so a read can skip files that cannot contain the key, avoiding a disk seek. Web caches and spell checkers have used the same trick.

search_results.title: Why you can't delete from a Bloom filter
search_results.snippet: Clearing a bit to remove one item could also remove other items that share it, creating false negatives. A counting Bloom filter replaces each bit with a small counter that is incremented on insert and decremented on delete, at the cost of more memory.

search_results.title: A short history of the Bloom filter
search_results.snippet: Burton Howard Bloom described the structure in a 1970 paper about space/time trade-offs in hash coding with allowable errors. His example was hyphenation: keep the rare words that need special rules in a compact filter.
